label_scope: Fixed implementation and complete public domain; no label changes with seed, routing or output.
classification: Purpose-built small T4 adaptation of vLLM routed grouped-GEMM. case_119 is a synthetic tail-group tile decoder regression, NOT an upstream historical bug.

source.copyright: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
source.preserved_mechanism: Stable expert grouping with sentinel padding; grouped GEMM program-id mapping; token input via original flattened route id // top_k; multiply original route weight; scatter to original route row; top-k sum.

adaptations: Extract one expert projection, not a complete nonlinear MoE layer or routing algorithm. Matrix storage is [E,K,N]; fixed dimensions, T4-compatible FP16 inputs and FP32 accumulator/output.
Replace vLLM custom C++ route alignment with public PyTorch stable sort/count/prefix/pad preparation of the same semantic buffers, removing a project runtime dependency.
Use exact padded allocation rather than an upper bound plus device num_tokens_post_padded. Empty experts produce zero blocks; all real routes are included once.
Choose GROUP_M=1 for fewer than four row tiles, otherwise GROUP_M=4; fixed BM16 BN32 BK32, no tuning or quantized path.
Zero initialize routed scratch, making missing-output counterexamples deterministic; no labels depend on allocator residue.
Remove bias, nonlinear activations, distributed expert maps and training; add full executable materialized-buffer contract and independent public FP64 token/choice reference.

synthetic_mutation.case_118: divide within-group program id by actual group_size_m
synthetic_mutation.case_119: divide within-group program id by nominal GROUP_M
synthetic_mutation.effect: A final group shorter than GROUP_M may repeat lower output tiles and omit higher output tiles. Full groups and one-column-tile grids can pass, but one legal missing-output witness rejects the whole implementation.

domain_rationale: One public contract for both versions; distinct top-k experts per token as normal top-k routing, any routing order/imbalance/empty experts, bounded finite ordinary materialized inputs. Input validation executes in run.

numerical_argument.exact_bound: For K<=129 and |x|,|w|<=0.5, each route has sum of absolute products <=32.25. Row weights are nonnegative with FP64 sum<=1; exact row sum can exceed one only by FP64 summation rounding (<4e-16). Consequently the weighted target is strictly below32.251 in magnitude, accounting for that tiny FP64 acceptance margin.
numerical_argument.rounding_bound: Use a conservative full-ulp FP32 unit2^-23, not an assumption of tensor-core round-to-nearest. gamma129(2^-23)*32.25 is about0.000496; FP32 route weighting and Q<=4 accumulation contribute less than0.00004, so ordinary-rounding error is below0.0006. Even conservatively flushing every subnormal FP16 operand incurs at most129*(2*0.5*2^-14+2^-28)<0.007875 additional absolute error. Combined error is below0.0085, within atol0.01. Intermediate route magnitudes remain at most32.25; the FP64 row-sum margin is negligible relative to the strict remaining margin. There is no FP16 output cast or nonlinear function.
numerical_argument.indexing_argument: Route preparation pads each expert separately, assigns every flattened route exactly once, and preserves its source and weight identity. Correct grouped mapping is a bijection for all bounded row/column tile counts. The final sum visits all Q route slots once.
numerical_argument.limitation: Reviewed algebra/error bound plus independent finite GPU qualification, not machine-checked proof. Mutation launches duplicate stores with identical computed values; concrete failure is an omitted nonzero tile, not race outcome or uninitialized data.

invalid_inputs.reason: x and expert-weight magnitudes must be at most 0.5
each token must choose distinct experts
materialized tensors without logical view flags required
ids must be int32 and route weights FP32
input storage ranges must be disjoint

cpu_audit.method: Exhaustive bounded tile-grid bijection; NumPy expert-major FP64 vs public token-major reference; actual public route preparation vs independent expert grouping.

gpu_probe_plan: 20 fixed plans; base, joint choice permutation and consistent expert relabel controls (where applicable). Cover 1..4 choices, empty experts, hot experts, shared experts across tokens, full/partial groups, N/K tails, zeros, cancellation, positive bounds and FP16 subnormals. All plans retained independent of model outcomes. One additional nonzero storage-offset contiguous input variation, with input byte ranges and fresh output storage checked on every call; total45 calls per implementation.
